newsitem.title: UK: UK's United News buys 20 pct stake in HTV.
newsitem.headline: UK's United News buys 20 pct stake in HTV.

text.p: Britain's United News & Media Plc said on Friday it had agreed to buy Scottish Television Plc's 19.9 percent stake in regional television company HTV Group Plc for 73.7 million pounds.
Britain's HTV Group, which operates the third television channel licence for for Wales and the west of England, conceded earlier this month that it might be a bid target.
United News said it regarded the agreement it had entered into with Scottish TV as an investment and had no plans to make an offer for the rest of HTV's share capital.

The group said it had also agreed to buy Scottish TV's holdings In Independent Television News Ltd (ITN), of which Scottish TV owns five percent. Buying all of this would give United News a 22 percent stake in news provider ITN.
Scottish TV is to receive 5.1 million pounds for its ITN stake.
"United and HTV already work together across a range of areas and this investment will strengthen the relationship," said United News in a statement.
"ITV (independent television) is the core of our broadcasting business," said Roger Laughton, chief executive of United Broadcasting and Entertainment.
"This investment gives us the opportunity to work more closely with HTV in the interests of strengthening the network as a whole," he said.
Scottish TV's holdings in HTV and ITN had at the end of June book values of 35.9 million stg and 1.1 million respectively.
"The disposal of our investments in HTV and ITN at a good premium will put us in a position of significant financial strength," said Scottish TV chairman Gus Macdonald.
"This flexibility will enable us to continue with our strategy of building a broader-based media business," he said.
